thread.title: Is Warren Buffett Adding To Apple Under $175? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Giovanni DiMauro
title: Is Warren Buffett Adding To Apple Under $175? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
The market is punishing Apple ( AAPL ) for removing sales guidance on iPhones. Apple has shed over 22% or $49 a share from the $220 level after reporting earnings on November 1st.
Apple has fallen into bear market territory; the game has changed. Wall Street is trashing market leaders as deep pockets continue taking profits after a multiyear rally for the ages.
Apple is not alone; all the FANG stocks are suffering, but today the focus is on Apple.
There are 100s of millions of Apple fans around the world. I would like to remind shareholders that the iPhone was a top seller on Alibaba ( BABA ) in China on Singles' Day November 11th.
I'm not going to go into a huge fundamental analysis as this article is about the mood of the market and technical factors being played out through programmed trading.
Apple has been a darling of Wall Street and with good reason. The company has a fantastic business model. They also have the number one investor in the world as a major shareholder, Warren Buffett.
At what price does Apple become a strong buy? That my investor friends, is the billion-dollar question. Is this sell-off different from others? It feels like it, but to be frank, I do not know. When in doubt, I go to the charts.
Below are two charts that are only different by a few days. The first chart of Apple was drawn on November 19th, after market close. I wrote an article on the 20th that was timely but not widely viewed
Here is the title.
Wall Street Is Systematically Taking Down Market Leaders I encourage investors to click here to read the article in full to see for yourself if my thesis has any merit.
Here is the 5-year weekly chart of Apple from Nov. 19th.
Investors can see I drew two lines of support where I think the stock could possibly trade over the coming weeks or months.
I believe in the power of charts and even more in the power of AI. (artificial intelligence). When the market turns south, volatility raises its ugly head, that’s when all hell can break loose.
When violent market events unfold, technical traders along with computer algorithms go to work on price discovery. What is price discovery? The decimation of a stock price caused by relentless selling until buyers step in.
Here is a 15-year weekly chart of Apple 3 days later on Nov. 23rd.
Each line drawn represents a potential target area for the share price. I highly encourage any active investors to click on the chart and ponder.
Granted the stock is in a sell-off, but what an epic run! Apple stock may be one of the greatest wealth creation vehicles in human history. I wish I would have been smart enough to buy Apple in 2005 when it was trading for $5.50 a share. I bought my first iPod in 2006 and guess what? It still works.
Apple is one of my favorite stocks. I believe it is the best company in the world! The main short-term problem for the company is the chart. This chart seems to be begging the computer algos to sell, sell, sell. Will the selling continue? No one knows for sure, what I do know is the market is dangerous and it will take out unhedged weak hands when least expected. The market can also destroy your hedge positions if not done properly.
Hedging an Apple trade When it comes to hedging, do not be fooled into thinking that the worst cannot happen, it often does and with regularity. One key factor is to make sure you give yourself enough hedge protection to the downside. Just because you're hedged doesn’t mean you're necessarily safe.
How I hedged a long Apple position today I bought Apple at $174, I wrote a covered Dec. 21st, $155 call option for $21.10 premium. In essence, I am selling my shares of Apple for $176.10 by December 21st.
If the stock drops to $160 by expiration date, I will have the shares called away and make only $2 a share. However, I may choose to buy more and average down. If the stock drops to $145, I keep the shares and keep the $21 premium, but am still upside down $4 a share. Without the hedge, I would be sitting on a loss of nearly $29 a share.
In this case, I am planning on buying more as it drops; if it falls to a level that I feel has a better risk reward.
In the chart below, I drew several potential levels that Apple could trade to over the next few weeks or months.
No one knows where Apple will trade on Monday, it's entirely possible that Apple turns around and rallies from the $172 level and goes back up over $200. Another possibility is that it slices through $164 and goes back to support around $150.
Is it too outlandish for a supercomputer program to trade Apple down to this level of $149? I think not; to my eye that doesn't even look like a line of solid support. Don't get me wrong, I am not even bearish on Apple, but I do believe the computer is going to find a way to get there. If $149 doesn't hold, then investors could see a quick trip to the next level of $119 in a huge bear market sell-off.
We now live in a world of AI and supercomputers. Why do you think these sell-offs have become so much more violent? My answer: AI Computer algorithms.
Here is a 2-year daily chart from today.
Bullish case In fairness to Apple, I believe they are the ultimate global company. They have built an ecosystem that supports their users' loyalty. They have a ton of cash and they are making an absolute fortune off their diversified service businesses.
I listened to the last earnings call and was blown away by the strength of their business model. $10B in service revenue for 90 days is a fascinating figure to this trader. Apple service revenue growth is the envy of the world up 31% YoY .
Here is a quote from the earnings report that is quite bullish.
“We concluded a record year with our best September quarter ever, growing double digits in every geographic segment. We set September quarter revenue records for iPhone and Wearables and all-time quarterly records for Services and Mac,” said Luca Maestri, Apple’s CFO. “We generated $19.5 billion in operating cash flow and returned over $23 billion to shareholders in dividends and share repurchases in the September quarter, bringing total capital returned in fiscal 2018 to almost $90 billion.”
Here is a clip showing guidance from the call .
The market is freaking out over management not reporting iPhone sales figures in the way analysts are accustomed. I think the selloff is currently overdone, but that doesn't mean it can't take a quick trip down to $165.
The company will be buying back millions of shares nonstop, so I do not think it will trade to $119. I would be surprised to see $150, but one should remember that Apple was trading there in February of this year.
The Buffett effect Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A ) (NYSE: BRK.B ) increased its stake in Apple to 252 million shares as of June 30 . The investment is worth more than $50B, making Berkshire the third-biggest shareholder in Apple according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Is he buying this current plunge? Investors will have to wait and see.
Bearish Case Apple has changed the way it reports total iPhone sales; analysts are freaking out about it. I don’t think it’s that big a deal; Apple is one of the best and most profitable company in the world.
Analysts are concerned that iPhone sales have reached their peak. That may be the case, but the service and Apple Pay transactions will continue to drive high margin profits. One cannot expect 30% gains on top of a record $10B service revenue in perpetuity.
Today's headline: Apple slices price of iPhone XR in Japan Is this bearish? Maybe I believe it all comes down to price. Apple is getting $750 for the iPhone XR in Japan and it has less options. Today's negative headlines took Apple to the $172 level.
Apple is now in a situation where headline risk can move the stock up or down. I would advise reading a little deeper into any headlines before selling on a knee-jerk reaction from a misleading article.
Finding the bottom of the new trading range is what I find most bearish about buying Apple stock. Everyone knows Apple is going to be buying their stock back. The question is: how far can the stock fall before it gaps up and rallies back to $200?
Conclusion Apple is in the penalty box for the moment, in part because of the shift in the way they report iPhone sales. The company is steering investors to focus on service revenue and overall total units sold.
The company reported on the last earnings call that they did more transactions with Apple Pay than PayPal in the quarter. Click here for the earnings release to read for yourself.
Apple is an earnings giant, growing revenue 20%, while returning $23B to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. In spite of that investors are worried that the earnings have peaked.
I believe bullish Investors must consider hedging at least part of any new positions in Apple. Options will drive the stock price, I see multiple strike prices being hedged as different strategies are in place.
Apple management will be buying back stock over the coming weeks and months thereby supporting the share price. In my opinion, the share price will find strong support around the $150 level.
I doubt Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway will be selling Apple anytime soon. He will likely use this weakness as an opportunity to add to the 252 million shares his company owns.
As always, I encourage investors to do their own research and make their own decisions. Don't let the talking heads of Wall Street scare you out of your shares. I believe it is imperative to have an exit strategy in place before making any trades.
